comment: Golden mutation-kind cases for MutationHarness. Each entry asserts that applying the named kind to `input_bytes_hex` at `byte_index` produces `expected_mutated_bytes_hex`. The harness loads these to verify its mutation engine matches the spec — independent of any connector parse step. Filed under flywheel_connectors-angoc.18.2.

kinds.note: Flip bit 7 (sign-bit) of 'H' (0x48) → 0xC8; same as HighBitFlip
Drop last 5 bytes from 'Hello World' (11 bytes) → 'Hello ' (6 bytes)
Truncate the entire input; harness should produce an empty slice without panic
Insert 0x00 before byte index 2; original 5 bytes become 6 bytes

result_classes.description: parse_fn returns Err(_) with a structured error type. The GOOD path: connector caught the malformed input.
parse_fn returns Ok(T) where T carries a field-level error variant. Connector parsed the envelope but flagged a bad field.
parse_fn returns Ok(T) from a mutation that only affected a truly-don't-care byte. Acceptable.
result_classes.ok_pattern: Ok(T) AND mutation_byte_position was in unused/padding region

result_classes.description: THE BUG: parse_fn returns Ok(T) with the mutated payload silently coerced or truncated. Mutation report flags this.
result_classes.ok_pattern: Ok(T) AND mutation_byte_position changed a load-bearing field AND error not surfaced

result_classes.description: parse_fn panicked. Hard fail; harness uses catch_unwind to recover and continue tallying.

expected_pilot_outcomes.note: Stripe charge response has amount + currency + status as load-bearing fields; silent coercion on any of those is operationally dangerous.
